items.text: Months from now, flyers for the Uluru Games will be drifting on the wind, bringing long-awaited good news to this city shrouded in thick fog.
But, the locals know nothing of it yet, including Liberti Grove. In East London, she finishes her knocker-upper work for the morning and makes her way home ... once more, on her own.
Before she makes a stop beneath a fateful eave.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: *chirps*

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: *chirps*?

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp, chirp?
Their cross-species interaction takes place on the corner, its participants oblivious to any onlookers, yet inevitably catching their eyes.

items.speaker: Classmate I
items.text: Oi, look who it is? It's Little Miss Why!

items.speaker: Classmate II
items.text: Hm? Is she trying to talk with that bird? Not surprised, two odd birds together.

items.speaker: Classmate I
items.text: You ain't half-wrong!
The children burst into laughter, roughhousing as they leave. Liberti looks back to the little blue bird on the eaves once again.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Don't pay them no mind. They're just like that.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Could be they're onto somethin', though. My bird-talk's a bit rusty, and you don't speak English neither, do ya?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Clocked you hangin' about a while ago. Been followin' me, have you? You fancy us being mates?

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: If you're tryin' to say "yes," then let's get a move on, eh?
Liberti's Home

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Shh. Keep it down. Mum don't care for being disturbed while she's workin'. She'll go on a proper rampage.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Just like this. Try to slip in through the window. Right.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Blimey, you actually came! So, I was right. You do wanna be mates.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Fancy some bread? It's all I've got for supper. Let's share it. Here, I'll break off some bits for ya.
The bird hops forward, peering over the bread with its beady black eyes before turning away.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Why? What's wrong? Don't care for bread?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Oh! A bit dry, innit? Hang on. I'll fetch ya some water.
Liberti turns to find her father leaning on the doorframe, rubbing his forehead, a tired look on his face.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Liberti, you're back.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: You up, Dad? Why you rubbin' your head? Still got a sore noggin'?

Her father came home late last night, knocking on the door in a drunken haze, and now looks as though he has only just rolled out of bed. Every night before his day off, he drinks with his coworkers "until the last drop's been drunk."
Liberti has never been fond of the sharp scent of alcohol clinging to her father, but she knows he isn't fond of it himself.
Her father says nothing in response.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Who you talkin' to?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: My new mate. See?
Liberti moves aside, introducing her father to the tiny guest standing on the windowsill.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: *sigh* You don't mean the bird, do ya? What am I to do with you, girl?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Why can't you be more like the other little'uns on the street, y'know, behave a bit more proper?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: They don't go off talkin' to birds all day. They go out and play with each other instead.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: But I don't like playin' with them.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: "Unsociable," that's what your teachers call you. Now, I've warned you already. You can't go on acting like this and do strange things.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: What do you mean "strange things"?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: *sigh* You always gotta mouth back to me, eh?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I still don't get it. I weren't mouthin' off, Dad. I just don't see why—
The door inside is flung wide open, hitting the wall with a loud thud.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Shush! Must you two make such an awful racket?
The true head of the Grove household stands in the doorway, exuding a silent, threatening aura. The pair go quiet at once.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Sorry, Mum.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: You know that while you're off having fun at school, I'm working myself to the bone, don't ya?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: From the second I open my eyes, it's naught but sewin' and weavin' for me! All day long! I'm gonna make myself blind from all this work!

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: So all I want's a bit of peace! Is that too much to ask?
Father and daughter bow their heads, silently saying a quiet prayer that this storm might pass over them.
However, the storm has other ideas. Mother's gaze suddenly hardens, fixing in place.
Liberti watches in confusion as she steps closer, inch by inch, until she finally stops at the windowsill, staring in disbelief at the half-eaten bread and the little bird perched nearby.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: What were you thinking, Liberti? Feeding your bread ... to a bleedin' bird?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I ... I ... It's only a bit of my supper, and I don't mind sharin'! It's just that she's my new mate, and I just thought I'd give her somethin'—

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Oh, don't mind sharing, do we?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Miss Liberti Grove, our own little Lady Bountiful, givin' out our bread to the poor little bird!

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: We don't work as hard as we do for you to feed your bird!

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp, chirp!
Liberti's new friend flits away from the window—a little disloyal, perhaps, but Liberti knows she can't be blamed.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Ease up. I'm sure Liberti knows she did wrong. And she won't be doing it again, will she?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Liberti, how about you go and fetch next week's shopping? Lend a hand around here, eh?

items.speaker: Father
items.text: Go get some money from your sister. I wrote the shoppin' list in a blank spot on the newspaper. Right here. Go on, off you trot!
The shopping list is shoved into Liberti's hand, and she is pushed out the door.
Unfortunately for her, council house doors are not known for their soundproofing.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: That girl can't keep carryin' on like this. You've got to talk some sense into her.

items.speaker: Father
items.text: I've told her time and again, but does she ever listen?

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp.
The lilting sound of a bird reaches her ears from above. Liberti looks up, her smile returning once more.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Waitin' for me, were you? Thanks. I was in need of some cheerin' up after all that.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Sorry. I hope they didn't give you too much of a fright. They ain't always so cross.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I'm off to find Sarah, my sister. She's usually down here with her union lot. You could wait with me if you like.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp.
Satisfied by the bird's answer, Liberti heads up the stairs. Just as she's about to knock, a large, broad-shouldered worker stops her.

items.speaker: Worker
items.text: Hey! What d'you think yer doin'? This ain't no playground, girly!
The worker eyes Liberti suspiciously, to him she's just another little mischief maker sneaking around and stirring up trouble. That is, until he hears the name of another "grown-up."

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I'm here for Sarah.

items.speaker: Worker
items.text: Right! I remember you, the little sister, ain't ya? 'Ang on then. I'll fetch her.
He motions toward Liberti, wordlessly impressing that she should stay by the entrance.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I don't like it much in there. Everyone's got faces redder than slapped backsides.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp, chirp?
Waiting at the door, she and the bird resume their friendly chatter.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I think Sarah's proper clever, and I do look up to her. Only ... sometimes I think she don't much care for me.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Mum and Dad were saying that Sarah's running for union leader. And if she wins, then she might move away.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: If she leaves, then I won't get to see much of her anymore. I don't know if that'd make me feel chuffed or gutted. Just thinkin' about it makes me feel a bit funny inside.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp, chirp!
The little bird perched above tilts its head and flutters down, landing softly on Liberti's drooping shoulder.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Oi! What are you like?! That tickles, haha!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: By the way, sorry about the bread. I hoped you'd get a bit more than you did. And I was plannin' to introduce you to Ollie. S'pose it'll have to wait till next time.
Liberti and her avian companion wait at the stoop of the doorway for a long while, and a touch of boredom begins to set in.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Oh, I know! How about I show you a bit o' magic? You up for that?
She reaches into her pocket for the half-sheet of newspaper, flattens it carefully, and pinches a corner, making the entire sheet stand upright.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Watch close now.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Stop! What are you doing?
A hardened hand, thick with calluses, seizes Liberti's wrist, sending the shopping list tumbling to the ground.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: You really doing "that" again? How many times have we—ugh, again and again—don't do "that"!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I-I ... was only ...

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: You haven't been doing that little trick of yours around town, have you? Trying to get some attention? Showing off to your schoolmates? Your friends?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I haven't!

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: You'd better not have.
Sarah fixes Liberti with a hard look, then finally lets go of her reddened wrist.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Remember this now. Don't go causing trouble for our family.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: That ain't true. I ain't causing no trouble! I'm doing my part as a knocker-up, aren't I?

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Oh aye, very impressive. And you know what I was doing at your age? Working four jobs in all.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: That was after the war! Before then—well, you don't know nothing about how rough it was then. I was younger than you are now, but I still made sure I was always seen and not heard. You've no idea how hard we had to work to get us here.
Liberti's head drops once again.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirp, chirp.
The bird nudges her cheek with its wing, and once more, Liberti lifts her head.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Why do you always do that? Why you always goin' on about how things used to be?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: And why do you always tell me not to use "that"?

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: You wouldn't understand even if I explained. Just remember what I've told you. You'll appreciate it when you're older.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I don't get it. It's always "when you're older," but why that the way it has to be? If you've got all the answers, why don't ya just tell me now?

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: How is it you come up with so many questions? There's no why!
A few passersby begin to glance their way. Sarah clears her throat and speaks more quietly.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Enough. I've no time for your usual nonsense. Just tell me what you're up to.
Without a word, Liberti reaches into her pocket and hands over the shopping list with a bended head.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: The shopping, is it? Well, it does need doing ... *sigh*
Her sister frowns as she digs into her pocket and counts out the coins one by one.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Here, this should do. And if the shopkeeper says it's short, you tell him he can forget about trying to charge us more!

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: And if there's any change, you bring it right back. No sweets, understand?
After giving her strict instructions, Sarah heads back inside, pulling the heavy door shut behind her.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I won't use it for sweets, honest.
Still, she plans to go to Mr. Laury's shop later, because she has to go home after the shopping's done.
For the time being, she has no desire to head home.
